input.quote: Such audit shall not occur more than [***] in a given Calendar Year, unless for cause, and shall not concern books and records relating to a period more than [***] preceding the current Calendar Year.
input.rationale: Section 9.9 (Audit Procedures) is the only audit right binding Sanofi as the audited party, and it is fully reciprocal. It meets the preferred position on each material term: (i) frequency is capped at a stated number of times per Calendar Year (p0416); (ii) advance notice is required ("at least [***] prior notice"); (iii) the audit must be performed by an "independent auditor of international prominence" reasonably acceptable to the audited Party, not by RevMed personnel; (iv) the auditor is expressly barred from disclosing the audited Party's Confidential Information beyond the payment discrepancy and must sign a confidentiality agreement with the audited Party (p0417, p0419); (v) the auditing Party "shall bear the full cost of such audit" unless the audit reveals an underpayment exceeding a stated percentage threshold, in which case the audited Party reimburses (p0418); and (vi) scope is limited to the books and records maintained under Section 9.8 (p0414) with a defined look-back period plus a waiver of stale claims — there is no right of direct or remote access to Sanofi systems, so the walk-away scenario is absent. Section 6.9 audit rights run in our favour (Sanofi auditing RevMed) and are out of scope. Two minor points are noted but not flagged: the frequency, notice, look-back and underpayment percentages are redacted ([***]) so exact figures cannot be confirmed against the 30-day / 5% preferred parameters, and the frequency cap carries an "unless for cause" exception. These are sub-elements short of ideal wording rather than fallback failures, and the clause's mutuality means any tightening would equally cut back our own audit rights over RevMed. No redline recommended; we should confirm the bracketed figures land at no more than once per Calendar Year, at least 30 days' notice and a 5% underpayment threshold when unredacted.
